title: Prospective evaluation of complications after percutaneous cannulation of the internal jugular vein for minimal invasive cardiac surgery
summary: The study aims to investigate the incidence of thrombotic events associated with cannulation of the internal jugular vein during the use of a heart-lung machine.

interventions.name:
Patients over the age of 18 who are undergoing minimally invasive cardiac surgery using a Cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB), in which the internal jugular vein is cannulated for this purpose. 
A control of the punctured internal jugular vein via sonography is carried out once, 72-96 hours after removal

Patients over the age of 18 who undergo minimally invasive cardiac surgery using a heart-lung machine (HLM) without jugular vein cannulation.
A single ultrasound examination of the punctured internal jugular vein is performed 72–96 hours after surgery.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Minimally invasive cardiac surgery using a heart-lung machine, with and without venous cannulation of the internal jugular vein
Exclusion criteria:
- Age <18 years
- Pre-existing occlusion of the internal jugular vein 
- Pre-existing thrombosis of the internal jugular vein 
- Known prothrombotic coagulopathy
- Catheterisation of the VJI within 14 days before surgery 
- Pre-existing anatomical anomaly of the internal jugular vein
